name: Niche directory website
one_liner: An AI-built directory of businesses in an overlooked niche, paid for by ads, paid listings and leads sold to the businesses listed.
customer: Businesses listed in the niche (for listings and leads) and advertisers
offer: Featured or subscription listings, display ads and qualified leads sent to listed businesses
how_it_makes_money: Ads, listing subscriptions and per-lead fees paid by listed businesses
startup_cost: low (~$10/month for the Abacus ChatLLM tool, plus a domain and hosting)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown (depends on SEO traffic; probably months)
evidence: 'You can monetize with ads, subscriptions, or you can collect leads organically and sell them to the businesses that are listed' (CKiszDu2aic)
'It used to take a developer months... today we can do that in minutes' (CKiszDu2aic)
No revenue figures given, so evidence is weak
risks: Depends on SEO, and AI search answers are taking traffic away
No revenue proof in the video
Low barrier to entry means copycats
Listings must be kept up to date

name: Etsy printables / digital downloads shop
one_liner: Simple digital printables made once and sold many times on Etsy, chosen from search-volume data rather than guesswork.
customer: Etsy shoppers buying planners, templates and printables
offer: Instant-download PDF and template printables in many variations
how_it_makes_money: Per-item digital sales on Etsy with almost no cost per sale
startup_cost: low (Etsy listing fees plus a keyword-research tool subscription)
time_to_first_revenue: First sales within weeks; $1,000/month reached in 4 months
evidence: Cody Berman started a new Etsy store from scratch and 'it took all of four months to reach his first $1,000 months' (DG4yP9MACWk)
Has sold printables since 2018 and runs it as a numbers game with many simple variations (DG4yP9MACWk)
risks: Saturated market where prices keep falling
Depends on Etsy's algorithm and policies
AI makes products easy for anyone to copy
The income ceiling per shop is modest

name: Event iced-coffee cart
one_liner: A low-cost mobile iced-coffee cart that sells high-margin cold brew at festivals, markets and events.
customer: Attendees at festivals, markets and events
offer: Iced coffee poured in about 30 seconds a cup
how_it_makes_money: About $8 per cup against under $3 in cost; event pitch fees around $150
time_to_first_revenue: The first event, so days to weeks
evidence: 'By Sunday, the end of this festival, Mark had cleared $8,000 in pure profit' (FE7PZG_V7qE)
'Every cup... cost less than three bucks to make, he sells it for eight bucks' (FE7PZG_V7qE)
Small event with 80 people makes about $400; 'the cost for being wrong is gas money and 150 bucks' (FE7PZG_V7qE)
risks: Must be run in person; not async
Revenue is seasonal and weather-dependent in the UK
Needs UK food hygiene registration and trader licensing
Best pitches are competitive

name: Contractor outdoor storage yards
one_liner: Fenced land rented as storage yards to contractors and owners of large vehicles and equipment.
customer: Contractors, service businesses and homeowners with boats, trailers or equipment
how_it_makes_money: Monthly rent per yard, priced on net rentable square footage; the asset value rises once it is leased up
startup_cost: high (land ~$1M plus ~$2.5M build-out in the example; a 'no money' route through leasing or partnering was claimed)
evidence: 34 yards on land costing ~$1M, $2.5M build-out, 'going to be worth six and a half when it's leased up' (EHiyxR6TwWE)
Claims the owner works 5 hours a week and makes '$5-15k/month cash flow' (EHiyxR6TwWE)
Found customers by approaching vehicles at red lights (EHiyxR6TwWE)
risks: Needs a lot of capital or a complicated deal structure
UK planning and land-use restrictions
The 'no money' claim isn't backed up
Local and physical, so it doesn't scale quickly

name: Heritage/allergy-friendly dry food mix brand
one_liner: A direct-to-consumer brand selling a family-recipe dry mix (pancakes in the example) with dairy-free variants.
customer: Home cooks and families with dietary restrictions
offer: Bagged pancake mix in traditional and dairy-free versions
how_it_makes_money: Product sales of 15–20k bags a month, over $80k/month revenue
startup_cost: low to begin ($12.17 claimed), medium to scale (commercial kitchen, machinery)
evidence: 'We do about 15 to 20,000 bags a month' (DCEnzD0Vlxo)
Started with $12.17 and moved from home to a commercial kitchen (DCEnzD0Vlxo)
risks: Food-safety, allergen and labelling rules (UK FSA)
Physical inventory and logistics
Hard to get noticed against CPG competitors
Founders said mistakes 'almost cost us everything'

name: Offshore pre-development design back office
one_liner: Spec and pre-development plans for property developers, drawn by a remote team of architects and engineers in a lower-cost country.
customer: Property developers and investors planning multifamily or historic redevelopments
offer: Pre-development feasibility and spec plan packages
how_it_makes_money: Per-project fees with a margin on remote labour (pricing not stated)
startup_cost: medium (needs a vetted remote professional team)
evidence: Weak: 'we launched Bolt Builders... back office of architects and engineers in Latin America... pre-development plans... for multifamily and historic' (D2Oek_YVIFA)
risks: Professional liability and local planning/code sign-off
Hard to win developer trust without a track record
Weak evidence
